title: Enhancement of Li and Na Storage in Janus HfSSe Monolayers by Co-Induced Electron-Deficient Chalcogen Sites: A First-Principles Study
authors: Md. Muktadir Hasan, Md. Mafizul Islam, Ahmed Zubair
abstract: The growing demand for high-capacity, fast-charging, and durable rechargeable batteries has intensified the search for advanced electrode materials, with two-dimensional materials offering large surface-to-mass ratios and short ion-diffusion pathways. Here, pristine and Co-doped Janus HfSSe monolayers were investigated as anode materials for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries using first-principles density functional theory. Pristine HfSSe was found to be dynamically stable and exhibited a 0.85 eV band gap, while Co substitution shifted the Fermi level toward the valence-band region. Adsorption of the first Li or Na layer induced metallic behavior, thereby improving charge transport. Co doping strengthened alkali-metal binding, with the most favorable Li and Na adsorption energies changing from -2.6125 and -1.9800 eV to -3.7405 and -3.0529 eV, respectively. Co doping created electron-deficient sites that enhanced Li/Na binding. Co-doped HfSSe accommodated up to four Li layers and three Na layers, increasing the theoretical capacities from 555.43 to 776.19 mAh/g for Li and from 370.29 to 582.14 mAh/g for Na. The average open-circuit voltages were 0.62 V for Li and 0.29-0.30 V for Na, with minimum migration barriers of 0.2153 and 0.1044 eV, respectively. These results identified Co-doped Janus HfSSe as a promising anode material for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries.
summary: This theoretical study investigates Co-doping in Janus HfSSe monolayers to improve their use as anode materials for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries. Using DFT, the authors demonstrate that Co doping strengthens alkali-metal binding by creating electron-deficient sites, leading to significantly higher theoretical storage capacities and maintaining fast ion diffusion pathways.
main_problem: The research addresses the critical need for advanced, high-capacity, and durable anode materials for next-generation rechargeable batteries, specifically for Li-ion and Na-ion systems.
main_result: Co-doping the Janus HfSSe monolayer significantly enhances its electrochemical performance, leading to increased theoretical capacities for both Li and Na storage and maintaining favorable ion diffusion kinetics.
method: The study employs first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations, including structural optimization, phonon calculations, and the CI-NEB method for diffusion barriers.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Janus HfSSe monolayer, which is computationally modified by substituting Cobalt (Co) atoms. The investigation compares the pristine material against the Co-doped variant.
key_observables: Alkali-metal adsorption energies, theoretical specific capacities ($	ext{mAh g}^{-1}$), average open-circuit voltages ($	ext{V}$), and minimum ion migration barriers ($	ext{eV}$).
important_parameters: The doping level and the resulting electron-deficient sites created by Co substitution are key parameters influencing binding strength.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on DFT approximations (PBE functional, DFT-D3 correction) and assume that the calculated electronic and structural properties predict real-world electrochemical performance.
figures_summary: Figures likely illustrate the optimized structure, phonon dispersion, adsorption energy comparisons (pristine vs. Co-doped), and electronic structure (band structure/PDOS) for the materials.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of problem identification (battery anode need), material selection ($	ext{HfSSe}$), computational methodology (DFT details), detailed results showing the effect of Co-doping on binding energy and capacity, and a final conclusion identifying the material as promising.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state electrochemistry, the use of first-principles methods to model charge transfer, electronic structure changes upon doping, and ion transport barriers is highly relevant to understanding correlated electron behavior in engineered quantum materials.
